text.p: Hungary's overnight interbank interest rates continued this week's trend of easing on a liquid market and closed slightly lower on Wednesday, dealers said.
"Today the deals were made at around 19.75 percent to 19.875 percent," said Istvan Zsoter of Takarekbank.
The overnight rates finished at 19.75 percent, compared with Tuesday's closing of 19.875 percent.
Traders said Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy's Tuesday announcement to cut the monthly devaluator to one percent from 1.1 percent on August 15 did not influence the money market.
"This does not affect the interbank market, rather the securities market where the yields went down on the news immediately," said Zsoter.
Government securities benchmark yields dropped by six to 11 basis points for all maturities on Tuesday.
Traders added that funds were flowing back from matured one-month reverse repo deals struck before a 50 basis point cut in most central bank repo rates on June 13.
Interest payments on government bonds issued in Hungary's banking consolidation programme - which recapitalised banks - also boosted market liquidity in the past few days, dealers added.
